chapter: Band family, war years and wrap-up
title: How 'Tippin' In' was recorded
summary: Bobby Smith wrote it, named for a dog, and recorded in Chicago.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, we was in Los Angeles. Bobby Smith, he penned that. And we, when he finished it, we rehearsed it out there.
He named the tune cause he had a dog he used to call Tippier. And that's where he got that "Tippin' In".

Well, we was playing it on those one nighters. On my way back to New York, I had to go through Chicago, so I called my office cause the more I played it and the more I heard it, I enjoyed it better. So, I called my office. I said make an engagement, a stopover at Victor in Chicago so I can record. You know, I said I've got something I want to record before I get to New York.
And, they did that. So, I did "Tippin' In", "Hawk's Boogie", "Remember". Now, the 4th number I don't remember just what it was.
We did this in Chicago. We finished that there, got back on the train, and came back on to New York. I couldn't wait to do it before I got back to New York. You know?
And that's how that came out. But I just, Bobby penned it but (inaudible) my solo, the trumpet solo and stuff that I did on
it. I just kept in and I just kept changing it practically every night till I just figured out what I want. When I got there, I just stayed on that one cause he left those openings in there for me.
